newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RESULTS TODAY - AFRICA, MINING TO LIFT LTA.
newsitem.headline: RESULTS TODAY - AFRICA, MINING TO LIFT LTA.

text.p: South African construction firm LTA Ltd's long reach north into Africa is seen the root of a sturdy 20 percent rise in half year earnings, offsetting a sluggish local building sector.
Analysts said that the big money-spinner in the group, which has already won projects across the continent, appeared to be LTA's widespread opencast mining work.
"They are just steaming ahead in Africa," said Nolan Menachemson, an analyst at SMK Securities.

"They have built up the expertise and critical mass necessary to tender for major opencast mining contracts and are expected to obtain a significant proportion of these contracts in the future," he said.
Analysts said that LTA had already secured projects on the gold mines in Mali, Ghana and Guinea and a wide range of work in countries including Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Lesotho.
And work in Africa looked set to grow with the group committing an estimated 200 million rand per year for capital expenditure.

In January LTA was part of a consortium, which also includes French firm Degremont (part of Lyonnaise de Eaux ) that sealed a 240 million French franc contract to build three treatment plants to supply drinking water to the Botswanan capital Gaborone.

But analysts said that LTA, along with other South African construction firms, had had a tougher time on its homefront as some work was delayed by heavy rains in March and a large number of public holidays.
"The local markets are not so wonderful, especially the building side although civil engineering is okay. LTA's earnings should be higher in the second half of the year," another analyst said.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast LTA's earnings for the six months ended June 30 rising to between 107.0 and 110.0 cents a share with consensus at 108.3 cents -- an increase of over 20.0 percent of the interim period a year ago.
They expected the dividend to come in at around 24.0 cents from 20.0 before.

Other positives in the group was a declining trend in its working capital requirement levels and its ability to provide a total turnkey operation, from the feasibility stage of a project, through to the process engineering, construction and the actual management of the contract.
